q: I take meticulous notes and every time I think I notice a pattern, he proves me wrong the next night. I feel so fixated on his schedule. And I’m so exhausted from not sleeping more than 2 hrs a time. I just started working this week so that’s a whole added stressor.
cx: Title: "Obsessed with the schedule". Six-month-old trained successfully, now waking every 1-2 hours.

q: It’s just hard because my husband and nanny both aren’t great at stretching his wake windows so I feel like I have to be “in charge” to make that change a reality. And I already have so much on my plate.
cx: Planning a move to two naps.

q: I’m not ready to sleep train MOTN wakings as we shared walls with neighbors and it’s just too hard for me to hear him cry in the middle of the night. But I also read here that night wakings are generally a schedule issue if independent sleep has been established.
cx: Same post; why middle-of-the-night training is off the table.

q: Baby went from impossible to transfer to crib to putting himself to sleep with minimal crying (sometimes none), including for night wakings. Thanks to everyone in this community who has commented on my posts.
cx: Credits the subreddit, not a paid programme, for the first success.

q: He cried for 50 minutes but then fell asleep. He only slept for 50 minutes and then awoke again.  I can’t imagine continuing to have him cry for 50 minutes to only get that amount of sleep, but don’t want to encourage crying or the nurse to sleep association.
cx: Extinction worked at bedtime for 3 weeks; first try overnight with a 4.5-month-old.

q: At which point it’s usually around 3:30 or 4 and I end up just rocking him until 5:30 am.
cx: The second half of every night.

q: Last night she was up screaming and throwing everything in her room from 12-220am. Obviously I have learned my lesson not to go in, but it’s also exhausting.
cx: Three-year-old, pacifiers taken away in August; now midnight screaming.

q: My 17 month old is still waking up throughout the night so often that it’s effecting my mental health and my mood is effecting my husband.
cx: Nursing and cosleeping a 17-month-old; considering weaning.

q: the next two wakeups I didn’t offer the boob she cried but shortly went back to sleep. By 3am I was just too tired so we nursed. Same thing at 6am.
cx: First night trying not to nurse at wakings.

q: We have also tried the cry it out method twice, but she gets so worked up she starts gurgling and choking on her spit so it’s simply not safe.
cx: Five-month-old wakes on every crib transfer, sometimes 7+ attempts.

q: Sorry for the book, but I’ve been watching all the videos with tips and tricks and it’s things we’re already doing… has anyone else experienced something like this and do you have any tips outside of cosleeping or contact napping?
cx: Same post; free video tips exhausted.

q: It was glorious.   I started to feel like myself again.   I was creative and energetic.   She was in such a good mood when she woke up.
cx: Remembering ten days when her baby slept through and took two long naps, two months ago.

q: It’s much harder to be content now. I’ve had a taste of the good life. I miss it. […] Anyone else had their sanity back only to be snatched away again? 🥲
cx: Now back to 30-minute naps.

q: Is night weaning the answer? How do I do it without letting him cry it out? Currently when he wakes I immediately comfort and feed him. This happens anywhere from 3-5 times a night (I have a mini fridge with bottles next to bed)
cx: Fifteen-month-old takes 16-24 oz overnight and soaks through diapers.

q: Before you ask, yes we went to a pediatrician but they were at a loss for an explanation and just said she was maybe a fussy baby.
cx: High-needs three-month-old sometimes needs three hours of holding while screaming to sleep.

q: We’ve been sleep training for weeks and genuinely aren’t seeing any improvement. She can fall asleep independently, so I feel like we’ve made progress there, but the cycle of hourly wake-ups after 2–3am just will not end.
cx: Five-month-old at daycare; second child; up every hour after 3am.

q: We are exhausted and starting to feel like we’re stuck in a vicious cycle of crappy nighttime sleep → crappy daytime sleep → crappy nighttime sleep.
cx: Same post.

q: Everything I read says 3-4 hours a day and early morning wakings have to do with being overtired?
cx: Commenters suggested too much daytime sleep.

q: Previous generations had whiskey and Orajel. What do we have? No seriously, what do we have?
cx: Eight days of molar teething: terrible naps, waking miserable.

q: I've tried to let him CIO before but the crying went on for 90 minutes before I intervened. He gets into hysterics pretty quick when left in his crib. I don't think sleep training will work for us, but I don't know what will. Please help
cx: Seven-month-old waking hourly since four months; nursing to sleep and cosleeping no longer working.

q: He did his best to get her to sleep and did the same routines I do, but she was very upset and wound up crying herself to sleep on his shoulder after a two hour struggle. […] I feel awful. Is she going to be okay? Did I break my commitment to not using CIO?
cx: First night away from her nursed-to-sleep 21-month-old, staying with her hospitalised mother.

q: She will kick away. She will scream until she's red, and I just want to know what's wrong. […] I really can't stand to hear her crying and not be able to comfort her in anyway.
cx: Four-month-old (adjusted) no longer settles even with a bottle; an hour of screaming per sleep.

q: My husband and I are going crazy room sharing with our 4 month old! We live in an old house with creaky hardwood and we’re fighting for our life tiptoeing in and out of the room every night!
cx: Baby startles awake at every sound; parents considering rugs and a new doorknob.

q: We don’t do cry it out or anything and come to him as soon as he cries so I’d like to be able to hear him.
cx: Why the baby stays in their room.

q: I asked her to run bloodwork to check my daughter’s iron - everything came back normal. This led to her saying my daughter just needed to be re-sleep trained.
cx: Nearly four-year-old with rage-filled night wakings since starting preschool; paediatrician's verdict.

q: we took my her to a specialist who has said she believes this is separation anxiety (she wants nothing to do with my husband at bedtime and in the night and responds much better to me). She’s given us a plan to help restore her confidence and get us to the point where we can sleep train again but…this is truly just miserable.
cx: Same post; a specialist's plan after the doctor's answer.

q: Exactly wondering the same. The fact that I don't know why is driving me crazy.
cx: Fifteen-month-old cries 1.5 hours 2-3 nights a week and takes milk 3-4 times nightly.

q: my husband has resorted to lying near the cot, initially with his hand on him and the last couple of times not needing to do this just lying there near him. and eventually he goes back to sleep and he sneaks out.
cx: Seventeen-month-old trained with CIO now wakes crying hard; dad does the resettling.

q: want it fixed and back to our previously good sleep asap but will CIO worsen things if it’s a separation anxiety phenomenon? or will it pass on its own and the gentler approach of being in the room is better?
cx: Same post; check-ins always wound him up before.

q: Posted here at 4 months and things got better for about a week in the 5 month window, but back again as I’m losing my mind and my temper.
cx: Six-month-old, horrible sleeper since birth; car naps on the nanny run.

q: We’ve let her try and cry it out during the night, but once it’s lasted 30+ minutes and she’s gasping for air and at a decibel i cant even describe, I’ve given up so she doesn’t wake out 3 year old.
cx: Why overnight cry it out stopped.

q: We have no other option for timing and how do you keep a baby awake in the car when you are the only person in the car?
cx: Thirty-minute nanny drive guarantees car naps that wreck the schedule.

q: My 3 year old had like a month regression at 6 months, we did sleep training, and he’s been great since. So I’m struggling.
cx: Same method that worked for her first isn't working now.

q: she won’t accept any dummy I’ve offered (and I’ve offered about 10 different types). I don’t know how to get her to fall asleep not on the boob.
